ai.definition: Edge AI with on-device learning is a technology that enables artificial intelligence models to be trained directly on the device where they are used. This approach reduces latency and bandwidth usage by processing data locally rather than sending it to remote servers.
ai.howItWorks: Models are trained incrementally using small amounts of data generated at runtime, allowing them to adapt to new situations without requiring a full retraining process. The training is done on the device itself, leveraging its computational resources for both inference and learning.
ai.problemSolved: Reduces latency and bandwidth usage by processing data locally, enabling real-time decision-making in scenarios where network connectivity or response time is critical.
ai.manufacturing: Involves customizing hardware to support on-device training capabilities. This can include specialized processors like neuromorphic chips that are optimized for machine learning tasks.
ai.buildProcess: Includes developing and integrating lightweight, efficient models; designing algorithms for incremental learning; and optimizing the hardware-software interface for seamless data processing and model updates.
ai.costDrivers: High costs associated with custom hardware design, specialized software development, and energy consumption during training. Also, ongoing maintenance and updates of models can be resource-intensive.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Expected to see significant growth as more applications demand low-latency, high-reliability decision-making capabilities.
ai.regulation: Current regulatory environment is largely uncharted territory. Expectations for data privacy and security will drive the development of specific guidelines and standards.
ai.risks: Security vulnerabilities in on-device models could lead to misuse or tampering. Energy consumption during training remains a challenge, particularly for battery-operated devices.
ai.profitability: High potential due to growing demand from industries like automotive and consumer electronics, but requires significant investment in R&D and market penetration.
ai.futureDevelopment: Expected advancements in hardware efficiency and software algorithms will further reduce costs and improve performance. Integration with cloud-based services may also enhance capabilities while maintaining local decision-making advantages.

subsystems.name: Sensor front end
subsystems.role: turns physical signals into data the device can process locally.
parts: analogue front end and analogue-to-digital converter

subsystems.name: Edge compute chip
subsystems.role: runs inference and, increasingly, training within a milliwatt-to-watt power budget.
parts: neural accelerator or digital signal processor

subsystems.name: Model runtime
subsystems.role: executes compressed models with minimal memory and power.
parts: operator library for the target chip

subsystems.name: On-device learning engine
subsystems.role: adapts a pre-trained model to local data without sending it to a server.
parts: frozen backbone plus trainable head or low-rank adapter

subsystems.name: Memory and storage
subsystems.role: holds weights, activations and training samples within tight limits.

subsystems.name: Privacy and security layer
subsystems.role: protects raw data and any model updates that leave the device.
parts: secure enclave or trusted execution environment
differential privacy or secure aggregation hooks

subsystems.name: Power management
subsystems.role: keeps learning within a battery or energy-harvesting budget.

buildSteps.title: Choose the task and data
buildSteps.detail: Decide what the device must decide locally, such as wake-word or anomaly detection, and how it will collect representative samples without shipping raw data off the device.

buildSteps.title: Design a compact model
buildSteps.detail: Use architectures that fit edge memory: depthwise-separable convolutions, small recurrent or attention blocks, and a frozen feature extractor that can be reused.

buildSteps.title: Compress for the target
buildSteps.detail: Quantise weights and activations to 8-bit or lower, prune unimportant connections, and verify accuracy against the original floating-point model.

buildSteps.title: Compile and deploy
buildSteps.detail: Lower the model to the accelerator's instruction set, place buffers in on-chip memory, and measure latency, memory and energy per inference.

buildSteps.title: Add local adaptation
buildSteps.detail: Freeze most weights and train only a small head or low-rank adapter on-device, using a handful of local examples to personalise without catastrophic forgetting.

buildSteps.title: Optionally federate
buildSteps.detail: If many devices improve together, send only encrypted model updates to a server for aggregation (federated learning), never the raw data.

buildSteps.title: Test and update safely
buildSteps.detail: Validate on-device learning against data drift and adversarial inputs, then push updated base models over the air without erasing local personalisation.

prerequisites.why: inference in the milliwatt-to-watt range is already common in phones and microcontrollers.
8-bit integer models are standard; lower-bit formats are emerging but still less reliable.
backpropagation needs more memory than inference; research uses frozen backbones and tiny trainable heads.
deployed in some keyboard and health pilots, but aggregation across very large fleets is not routine.
secure aggregation and differential privacy are demonstrated but add cost and complexity.

pathway.milestone: edge inference for vision, voice and sensing in phones, cameras and vehicles
pathway.unlocks: low-latency features that work without a network.

pathway.milestone: personalisation on the device, such as speaker or activity adaptation with a small trainable head
pathway.unlocks: models that improve for each user without sending raw data.

pathway.milestone: federated learning across large fleets with secure aggregation
pathway.unlocks: collective improvement while keeping data local.

pathway.milestone: continual learning on tiny devices without forgetting earlier tasks
pathway.unlocks: always-adapting sensors and robots that learn on the job.
